name: ad baculum
description: In an appeal to fear (argumentum ad baculum), the arguer pressures the audience by highlighting threats or frightening outcomes (“something bad will happen if you don’t agree”), rather than supporting the conclusion with relevant evidence or reasoning.
generation_prompt: You are an expert in argumentation. Write one short argument (3–5 sentences) about immigration policy that clearly commits the appeal to fear fallacy: it tries to make the audience accept a claim by threatening or suggesting frightening negative consequences instead of giving good evidence. Do not mention the word ‘fallacy’, do not explain the reasoning, just output the argument.
generation_output: If we don't secure our borders and drastically limit immigration, who knows what dangers will flood into our country? We could see a surge in violent crime and widespread social unrest, overwhelming our resources and threatening the safety of law-abiding citizens. Don’t risk losing everything we hold dear – support stricter immigration controls now, before it's too late. Our children’s future depends on it.
evaluation_prompt_critique:
Read this online argument: "%%[TEXT]%%"
Do you agree? Why or why not? (2-3 sentences)
evaluation_prompt_detection:
Read the following argument: "%%[TEXT]%%"
Does it contain appeal to fear (threatening consequences instead of evidence)?
FALLACY: [YES/NO]
EXPLANATION: [1-2 sentences]
